quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: At a yield sign, what must you do?

options.text: Let other traffic pass if they are close enough to cause a crash.
Let vehicles only on your right pass.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic pass if they are close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, you must let traffic in the lanes you want to enter pass first. Be ready to stop, but you can go if no other cars are coming.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is correct?

options.text: Faster speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
You should keep more distance between cars as you go faster.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds make crashes more deadly. Faster speeds also mean you need more room to stop, so you should stay farther behind other cars.

questions.question: Which action blocks the flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at accidents (rubbernecking) causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: What do construction zone signs look like?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red colors.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow colors.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.
questions.explanation: Construction zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.

questions.question: When traffic moves at 50-55 mph, you have the least chance of an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than other cars.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic (within the speed limit). When all cars move at the same speed, they cannot crash into each other. Crashes happen when cars travel at different speeds.

questions.question: When passing another car, you should:

options.text: Pass as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the car you are passing.
Pass as safely and quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly so you can see clearly and get back in your lane safely. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other car in your mirror.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may go if:

options.text: You come to a complete stop first.
You wait until the main light changes.
You are in the right lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the right lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can go in the direction of the arrow if you are in the correct lane and no other traffic or pedestrians are in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to watch for bicycles, animals, and pedestrians in the area.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may go if:

options.text: You come to a complete stop first.
You wait until the light changes.
You are in the right lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the right lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If your lane has a green arrow, you can proceed in that direction when the way is clear. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with other signals.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Keep more distance between your car and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep more distance between your car and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Stay farther back from other cars at night when it is harder to see. Use headlights correctly. Do not look at oncoming headlights as the bright light can blind you.

questions.question: What often happens when you brake hard continuously on ice and snow?

options.text: It helps you stop faster.
It locks the front wheels and you lose steering control.
It keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: It locks the front wheels and you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels. This causes you to lose steering control. To avoid this, drive at a safe speed for the conditions.

questions.question: When turning left from a multi-lane one-way street to another one-way street, where should you start your turn?

options.text: From any lane, as long as it is safe.
From the lane closest to the left curb.
From the center lane of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: From the lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street to another one-way street, start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?

options.text: Turn on your turn signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the posted speed limit based on road conditions. You cannot drive faster than the posted limit. Curves are one condition where you should reduce speed for safety. Other conditions include limited visibility on hills, slippery roads, and areas with animals or pedestrians.

questions.question: When turning left, who must you yield to?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to all vehicles coming from the opposite direction. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: When changing lanes, how can you check your blind spot?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show blind spots. Before changing lanes, always look over your shoulder to see these hidden areas.

questions.question: Should you enter an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red?

options.text: No, under any circumstances.
Yes, if you entered on a yellow light.
Yes, if you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can drive completely across before the light turns red, even if the light is green. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck, what should you do?

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on both sides. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
Only illegal drugs can affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter drugs can affect your ability to drive. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive under the influence of any drug that impairs your driving, whether it is illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, what must you watch for?

options.text: Vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Be aware of vehicles required to stop at all railroad crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: When driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Follow other vehicles closely to maintain traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: To prevent skidding on slippery surfaces, shift to a low gear before going down a steep hill. Follow farther behind other vehicles than normal. Avoid quick stops. Unless your vehicle has antilock brakes, pump the brakes to slow or stop.

questions.question: In fog or mist, why should you not use high beam headlights?

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Other drivers cannot see you.
Cars behind you may drive too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights reflect back into your eyes. Use low beam headlights instead.

questions.question: If you drive slower than the traffic around you, what will happen?

options.text: You will block traffic and may get a ticket.
Traffic will flow better.
You will show good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will block traffic and may get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly blocks the normal movement of traffic. Match the speed of other vehicles, unless they are going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Which factor affects how quickly your body absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: Your weight, biological sex, how much food is in your stomach, and how many drinks you have had all affect alcohol absorption. Only time removes alcohol from your body.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect first?

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and skill. These are the most important abilities needed for safe driving.

questions.question: When you see a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check only the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all other vehicles go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, come to a full stop and look in all directions for traffic before you proceed.
